name: VBScript
title: VBScript (6.0)
lifecycleNote: deprecated by Microsoft in 2024 and disabled by default

presenceList.meta: Ec3, Ec4, V3, D1, G1, Q3, Q4

type.text: **A variable has no declared type**: `Dim x` declares a name, and the value it holds is a `Variant` whose subtype is decided at the assignment, so the operator resolves the operands when the statement runs and `+` adds or concatenates according to the values it receives
**There is no namespace**: Every global variable and procedure lives in one flat global scope, so two included scripts share it
**There is no module boundary**: A script file exports nothing and imports nothing explicitly, and `ExecuteGlobal` or a `.wsf` include writes into the same global scope
**The subtype is inspectable**: `VarType`, `IsNumeric`, `IsDate`, `IsArray`, and `IsObject` let a script ask what a variant holds
**`Null` and `Empty` are distinct values with their own tests**: `IsNull` and `IsEmpty` separate a true null from an uninitialised variant
**`Class`, added in version 5.0, groups state with behaviour**: A class declares `Private` fields and `Public` property procedures, with `Class_Initialize` and `Class_Terminate`
Inherits the engine rule: string length counts UTF-16 units

construction.text: **A global variable appears at its first assignment**: Without `Option Explicit`, `x = 1` at file scope creates a global, so state appears wherever a name is first used
**`Option Explicit` requires a declaration**: With it, an undeclared name is an error instead of a new variable
**`Sub` and `Function` scope their own locals**: A `Dim` inside a procedure belongs to that procedure
**A class validates and cleans up in its two lifecycle methods**: `Class_Initialize` runs at creation and `Class_Terminate` at release
**A `.wsf` file combines several scripts**: A Windows Script File includes more than one script file, and the procedures of one are callable from another
**`ExecuteGlobal` defines a global at run time**: A generated statement can create a name that no declaration lists

memory.text: **The script engine owns the memory**: There is no allocate, free, or pointer operation in the language
**A COM object is released by reference count**: The object is freed when its last reference goes out of scope, and `Class_Terminate` runs at that point
**No pointer type and no address exist**: A value can never name a memory location
**A class instance is collected by the engine**: The script states no lifetime for a class object
**A reference cycle between script and COM objects is not reclaimed**: The engine's counter cannot release a cycle, and the process must end to reclaim it
**Repeated string concatenation in a loop reallocates**: A long string built with `&` is copied at each step, and the language has no string builder

error.text: **There is no structured error path**: The language has no `try` and no `catch`, only `On Error Resume Next` and the `Err` object
**`On Error Resume Next` discards a failure by default**: The next statement runs regardless, and the failure is invisible unless `Err.Number` is tested
**The `Err` object makes a failure a value**: `Err.Number`, `Err.Description`, `Err.Source`, and `Err.Raise` let a handler read and create a failure
**`On Error GoTo 0` ends the suppressed mode**: Error handling returns to the default at that statement
**A host error names its provider**: An ADO, WMI, or file-system failure carries a provider-specific number and source, so a handler is bound to that provider
**An unhandled failure ends the script**: There is no caller frame to unwind to, and the default action is to stop

concurrency.text: **The language has no shared-memory concurrency**: A script runs single-threaded in its host, so there is no race to guard
**A script can start another process**: `WScript.Shell.Run` launches a program, and `Exec` returns a stream of its output
**The host delivers an event to the script on its own thread**: A callback is serialised onto the host's thread, so the script never observes a concurrent invocation of itself
**The host decides the threading model**: Windows Script Host, Internet Explorer, and classic ASP each run a script differently, and the host's apartment model governs a COM call
**A session-scoped object is shared across requests**: In classic ASP, `Session` state is visible to more than one request, and nothing in the language partitions it
**A long-running script blocks its host thread**: The language has no yield and no cancellation

platform.text: **The engine is Windows-only**: `vbscript.dll` is the only implementation, and it ships with Windows, so a script runs on no other platform

**Every capability arrives through COM**: File access, WMI, ADO, and the shell are COM objects such as `Scripting.FileSystemObject` and `ADODB.Connection`, so a script depends on the registered object model
**A `.vbs` file needs no build step**: The host runs the text as written
**The host is part of the operating system**: `cscript.exe` and `wscript.exe` are installed with Windows
**The host decides which objects exist**: Windows Script Host, Internet Explorer, and classic ASP present different object models to the same language
**A `.wsf` file states its own includes**: A multi-file script needs the `Job` attributes and the `<script src=...>` elements that name its parts

performance.text: **The compiled form does not survive the process**: The engine compiles the script at load rather than ahead of time, so a fresh host pays the parse again
**A variant costs at every operation**: An operation reads the subtype tag and converts the operands before it acts
**The engine is an in-process library**: The host loads it once, so a script starts with no separate runtime to launch
**The engine compiles the file before it runs**: The host parses and compiles the script once at start, and a page host can keep the compiled script for later requests
**A COM call dominates a data-heavy script**: The crossing into ADO, WMI, or a file-system object is where the time goes
**String handling is the common trap**: Concatenation in a loop and a repeated `RegExp` replace on a large string cost far more than the control flow

ecosystem.text: **The language is proprietary and discontinued**: It exists in one vendor's product, and Microsoft announced the deprecation in October 2023
**The ecosystem is legacy and frozen**: The language has gained no feature since version 5.5 (2000), when the engine moved to sustaining engineering, so the tool field is historical
**The runtime tooling is part of Windows**: `cscript` and `wscript` are installed with the operating system
**A large body of published scripts exists**: Administrative scripts, examples, and books from the 2000s are widely available
**The migration targets are named and documented**: Microsoft points to PowerShell and JavaScript and describes the path
**Many environments block the script host**: A security policy or a mail filter commonly disables or rejects a `.vbs` file

evolution.text: **The language is discontinued**: Microsoft announced the deprecation in October 2023 with removal planned after 2027, so no further version is expected
**The remaining life is long and published**: The phased plan keeps the language available as an on-demand feature for years, so an existing script keeps running
**The language does not change under a script**: An existing script's meaning is fixed, which makes a migration predictable
**A successor covers each use**: PowerShell replaces the administration role and JavaScript replaces the browser and page role
**New code has no reason to choose it**: The direction of the platform is removal, not extension

domain.text: **The domain is Windows administration and COM**: The useful work is expressed through WMI, ADO, the file-system object, and the shell, and none of that exists off Windows
**Administrative automation fits it well**: A short script drives WMI and the registry directly
**Classic ASP and HTML Applications were real hosting domains**: A server page and an `.hta` file both used VBScript with the full object model
**Test automation still uses it**: UFT One and similar tools keep a VBScript dialect for their test scripts
**PowerShell has replaced it for administration**: The same task is now written in PowerShell
**An embedded operator interface is a narrow remaining use**: A few industrial and point-of-sale systems still run a VBScript engine for local automation

learning.text: **The syntax is small**: `If ... Then ... End If`, `Sub`, `Function`, and `For Each` are the surface
**The curve is gentle for a Visual Basic programmer**: The classic Visual Basic surface carries over almost unchanged
**The reference is complete**: Microsoft's VBScript Language Reference documents every statement and function
**The error model is easy to start with**: `On Error Resume Next` and the `Err` object are a few lines
**The real subject is COM**: The object model beneath the language is the large part of the work
**The error model is easy to misuse**: It requires a discipline that the language does not enforce

syntax.text: **The keywords are words**: `If`, `Then`, `Else`, `End If`, `For Each`, and `Next`
**A line is a statement**: Statement boundaries are lines, and `:` separates two statements on one line
**Line continuation is explicit**: `_` continues a statement on the next line
**A block closes with its keyword pair**: `End If`, `End Sub`, `End Function`, `Loop`, and `Next` each close their own construct
**The language is case-insensitive**: `myValue` and `MyValue` name the same variable, so a rename is not caught by the case
**`Dim` may be omitted**: Without `Option Explicit`, a name is declared by its first use, so a typo reads as a new variable

testing.text: **There is no test framework in the language or the host**: A check is a script that compares values and reports the result
**A test is a `.vbs` file run by `cscript`**: The same engine runs the test and the code under test
**A harness is only a few lines**: `WScript.Echo` with a comparison gives a report, and a failing check can call `Err.Raise`
**`cscript //X` starts the script debugger**: A step-through debugger is available where the Windows debugging tools are installed
**A test suite is the programmer's own**: There is no runner, no fixture loader, and no report format
**A type error appears only in the test run**: Nothing checks a value's use before the line executes

security.text: **Untrusted input can become code**: `Execute`, `ExecuteGlobal`, and `Eval` evaluate text, so a value built from input can run as a statement
**Script malware is a known, historical class**: The ILOVEYOU worm spread as a `.vbs` attachment, and the file extension is still commonly blocked
**The file-system object grants the user's own rights**: `Scripting.FileSystemObject` can read or overwrite any file the invoking user can
**A script runs without elevation by default**: It holds the privileges of the invoking user and no more
**The usual mitigation is policy**: A mail filter, an attachment block, or a group-policy restriction, rather than a language feature
**Correct quoting must be uniform**: An injection that forms a valid statement is not distinguishable from a legitimate one by the engine
Numbers are doubles: integers above 2^53 change value in silence

tradeoffs: **Hosted scripting is the purpose of the language**: VBScript is designed to be embedded in a host, so the dependence on the host is a scope decision
**The classic Visual Basic surface is a familiarity trade**: The BASIC syntax is easy to read, and one value type keeps the engine simple, at the cost of the type system
**A suppressed error is sometimes deliberate**: `On Error Resume Next` around one statement is a chosen tactic
**The language is meant for short programs**: A page of automation is the design point, not a system
**A fixed parameter list is a deliberate omission**: The language cannot pass a variable number of arguments, so a variadic call is written as an array parameter
**The deprecation is a lifecycle decision**: Microsoft's removal plan is a product decision rather than a language mechanism
verdict: VBScript holds the lowest pair of scores in this group, and the losses concentrate in its defaults and its dependence. A variable is a `Variant` with no declared type, an undeclared name becomes a global, an error is a mode the caller must enable, and every useful capability arrives through a COM object that exists only on Windows. What the language does provide is a tiny readable syntax, a host that is already installed, lifecycle methods on a class, and `Option Explicit` to require a declaration. Main strengths: a gentle learning curve, direct WMI and ADO automation, a `.wsf` file that packages a multi-file script, and a simple way to restrict a script through the Windows Script Host. Main weaknesses: no structured error path, no namespace and no module boundary, a proprietary and discontinued implementation, a domain locked to Windows and COM, weak tooling, and an injection surface that made it a malware vehicle.

energy.text: Runs on a virtual machine, above native code in the energy and time benchmarks [@pereira2017energy]; a causal re-analysis attributes most of the gap to execution time [@vankempen2025green].

ai-readiness.text: Sparse training data: models write it unreliably [@joel2025lowresource].

safety.text: No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.

delivery.note: The installed interpreter reads the source at run time; no compiled unit crosses a boundary
